title: Refund policy
content:
Fictional merchant support policy — evaluation fixture, not legal or financial guidance.

Customers can request a refund within seven days of delivery. The item must be unused and in its original packaging. Open the Returns section in the order page and select Request refund.

Approved refunds return to the original payment method within five to seven business days. Do not promise an instant refund. Damaged items require a photo and the order reference; escalate them to the support lead.

title: Delivery and tracking
content:
Fictional merchant shipping runbook.

Standard delivery takes three to five business days after dispatch. A tracking link appears on the order page after dispatch. If tracking has not updated for forty-eight hours, create a carrier investigation and send the customer its reference.

Customers can change the delivery address only before dispatch. Once an order has shipped, ask the carrier whether rerouting is possible; do not guarantee it.

title: Account security
content:
Fictional merchant account support runbook.

To reset a forgotten password, select Forgot password on the sign-in page. The password reset link expires after thirty minutes. Support must never ask for a customer's password or one-time password.

For suspected account takeover, lock the account temporarily and escalate to the security lead. Verify ownership through the established recovery process before restoring access.

title: Payment reconciliation
content:
Fictional merchant payment operations runbook.

When a payment is debited but the order remains pending, check the payment reference in the reconciliation dashboard. Allow twenty-four hours for the payment status to settle before raising an investigation.

For duplicate charges, record both payment references and escalate to the payments team. Do not initiate a second refund while a refund for the same charge is already pending.

title: Service incident response
content:
Fictional merchant service incident runbook.

For a checkout outage, declare a severity-one incident, notify the on-call engineer, and post a status update every fifteen minutes. The incident commander coordinates investigation and customer communication.

After service recovery, observe error rates for thirty minutes before closing the incident. Create a post-incident review within two business days and record corrective actions with owners.
